@graph.conditionsOfAccess: Open. No controlled-access data and no authentication anywhere in the workflow: every input is retrieved over HTTPS from a public archive (NCBI GEO, the source publication's supplementary files, the NanoString CellProfileLibrary, CellChatDB and UCSC Xena), each pinned by SHA-256 and re-verified on every run.
@graph.description:
A reproducible Snakemake workflow reanalysing NanoString GeoMx DSP whole transcriptome profiles from GEO GSE200563 (120 AOIs; 35 NSCLC patients plus 7 non-tumour brain controls; source publication PMID 36216799) to ask how the tumour immune microenvironment differs between a primary lung tumour and a brain metastasis, resolved by tissue compartment.
WHAT THE DESIGN CANNOT SUPPORT, stated here because a crate is read by people who will never open docs/limitations.md. The brain immune compartment is n = 8 AOIs, which detects roughly 1.1-1.3 SD at 80% power, so a null result in this study is UNINFORMATIVE, NOT NEGATIVE. Detection is the dominant limitation ahead of even that: three of six immune signatures and 40 of 63 checkpoint gene x compartment cells sit below the pre-registered detection floor. The assay carries NO COORDINATES — an AOI is a region a pathologist placed — so cross-compartment results are inferred crosstalk between adjacent compartments, never colocalisation. PanCK was the only collection mask, so a compartment label is never a cell-type label. This is a learning and methods project, not a publication.
@graph.name: Compartment-resolved spatial transcriptomics of the NSCLC tumour immune microenvironment: primary lung tumour versus brain metastasis

@graph.description: The Snakemake workflow itself — the target rules, one .smk per phase, the analysis scripts in both languages, the conda environment specifications with their osx-arm64 pins, and the schemas every manifest is validated against at parse time.
@graph.name: workflow

@graph.description: Every threshold, gene set, panel and pinned digest the workflow reads. The design table (samples.tsv) and the compartment vocabulary live here too, so the crate carries the study design and not only its code.
@graph.name: configuration

@graph.description: The read-only inputs and their provenance. resources/ has six sanctioned writers — raw/ (GEO), reference/ (SpatialDecon cell profiles), supplementary/ (the source publication's own deposited files), ligand_receptor/ (CellChatDB v2), clinical/ (Supplementary Data 1) and tcga/ (the TCGA-LUAD external cohort) — and each carries a *_checksums.sha256 and *_provenance.tsv pair recording what was fetched, from where, when, and at which digest.
@graph.name: inputs

@graph.description: The pinned input artifacts themselves, taken from the six fetch manifests rather than from a glob. raw/, reference/ and supplementary/ are gitignored — the digests are the provenance record and the bytes are re-fetchable — so on a fresh clone a glob over them matches nothing and the crate would describe no inputs at all while still validating. P6-T1 found precisely that, at parse time, before anything could run.
@graph.name: fetched_inputs

@graph.description: marimo notebooks (.py, never .ipynb), each with PEP 723 dependencies inlined so it runs standalone under uv. Review-tier notebooks are where a threshold was chosen; app-tier notebooks are the interactive artifacts. No reported number originates in any of them.
@graph.name: notebooks

@graph.description: The provenance record, the limitations, the analysis notes, the decision record (every ADR), the licences, the changelog and the citation metadata.
